crop.notes: Only the first column of the page-5 report: headlines, the excursion, who was there and picking up the men, ending at 'A Morning Call.' The rest of the page-5 text (columns 2–3, including 'The Fight') is not in the clipping; the round-by-round continuation on page 8 is article 468.

title.suggested: Tom Allen defeats Mike McCoole: the excursion

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen defeated Mike McCoole and described the steamer Continental's excursion of about a thousand people up the river, Allen boarding at Bissell's Point with seconds Arthur Chambers and Patsy Sheppard.

metadata.notes: Page 5 head reads '...PTEMBER 24, 1873'; the continuation page reads 'The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, Wednesday, September 24, 1873'. In 1873 the paper was the Missouri Republican, not the St. Louis Republic.

facts.fact: Allen defeated Mike McCoole on September 23, 1873, getting off 'with one scratch, and that on his knuckle'
About a thousand spectators went up the river from St. Louis on the steamer Continental for the Allen–McCoole fight, paying five dollars a head to Jack Looney
Allen boarded the steamer at Bissell's Point, with Arthur Chambers and Patsy Sheppard as his seconds; McCoole boarded at Sawyer bend with Tom Kelly
Ben Hogan, on board for the fight, was matched to fight Allen in thirty days

notes: The current title names Williams Island, but no battle-ground is named in the clipping, so the place could not be checked; the suggested title leaves it out. The headline is 'Mangled McCoole'.
